name: Raytraced 3D
description: Ray-marched or path-traced scenes in a WebGL2 fragment shader: signed-distance primitives, soft shadows and global-illumination look, with an automatic performance fallback ladder.

render.notes: Fullscreen triangle; scene as SDFs in GLSL; progressive accumulation when the camera is still; scale tiers chosen by a frame-time governor.

palette.notes: Physically-flavoured colours; tone-map and gamma at the end; keep a small named material table.

settings.note: characters are SDF blobs or sprites composited in 2D

fx.note: blue-noise dither hides banding and low sample counts

physics.model: CPU-side kinematics against the same SDF (mirror the GLSL in JS)
physics.notes: Keep a JS twin of the scene SDF for collision and tests.

worldgen.method: seeded parameter sets for SDF scenes

input.scheme: mouse look + WASD, or orbit camera

performance.fallbackTier: ladder: path-traced 1spp accumulate, then ray-march 1x, then 0.5x, then 0.25x with no soft shadows, then the lowpoly-3d preset

swarm.shape: small: one shader specialist (opus) and a few agents on gameplay/audio; shaders are hard to parallelise

verification: node --test passes (JS SDF twin matches expected values at sample points)
shader compiles and the info log is empty on the target GPU
frame-time governor drops tiers under a synthetic load
screenshot at each fallback tier is legible
a context-loss event leaves the page usable
pitfalls: GPU watchdog resets on long shader loops: cap march steps
integrated GPUs miss 60 fps at full res: enforce the ladder
no headless GPU: shots need a real browser
precision artefacts far from the origin

choices: progressive accumulation buffer (RGBA16F with float fallback)
limits: a handful of SDF primitives and 1-2 bounces
